title: Nothing Is Added
logline: In dry scrub and paddy country in the north, a rectangle of ground that has been fenced, taped and posted with warning boards for years is worked through lane by lane to full depth, sampled, surveyed, confirmed and signed off, and then the stakes are pulled, the boards unbolted and the tape wound onto a drum and carried away, so that the ground is left looking exactly like the ground beside it.
human_question: Why does the end of something weighing on you feel different in kind from being given something new?

place.what_kind_of_place: Flat, hot, lightly wooded country a few metres above sea level, in a district where the dry zone runs right down to a shallow coast. Thorn scrub and palu and weera on the higher ground, small tanks, rain-fed paddy in the low ground, sandy tracks, hamlets a kilometre apart, and long stretches where nothing is worked at all. Set into this, and visible only because it is the one part of the picture nobody has touched, is a marked rectangle: a boundary of short stakes with painted tops, a line of tape strung between them, and at intervals a board on two legs carrying a symbol and a word in three scripts. Inside it, scrub has grown to the height of a person while the land around it has been cleared, ploughed and cropped for a decade. At the edge stands the working arrangement: a lane cut in at right angles to the boundary, a marker at each metre, a detector, a trowel, a prodder, a sifting screen, a shade tarpaulin, a water can, a stretcher nobody expects to use, a radio, and a board on an easel with the day's cleared area chalked on it. Everything about the place is procedural. Nothing in it is improvised and nothing in it is quick.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because it is a place organised around a negative, and the negative is visible from the air and invisible from the ground. From height the whole concept is in one frame: worked land on every side, and inside it a rectangle of untouched scrub with a straight edge that no plant would ever make, and a thread of tape holding the straight edge in place. That shot is beautiful before it means anything: the geometry is absolute, the colour difference between worked and unworked ground is complete, and the eye goes to the empty box. At working distance the film is very small movements in a fixed order: a detector head swung in an arc the width of a body, a stake moved forward by exactly the length of what has been done, spoil going through a screen, a trowel going in sideways and not down, a hand signal, a pause, the same arc again. And the ending is the rarest thing a location can offer: an ending that consists entirely of removal. The fence comes out, the boards come off their legs and go into a vehicle, the tape is wound onto a drum, and the place stops being a place. The last shot of the film is the same frame as the first with nothing in it.
place.what_moves_or_changes: A boundary, inward, very slowly, and then all at once nothing. For years the rectangle only has its edge maintained: the tape is re-strung, the boards are repainted, the stakes are replaced, and the area does not change. Survey can shrink the box on paper before anything is cleared. Then clearance goes through it lane by lane, at a speed measured in square metres a day, and the cleared part is indistinguishable from the uncleared part except on the chalkboard. At the end comes a sequence that is all paper: sampling and quality assurance, a completion survey, a confirmation from the village officer that no contamination is known, and a district sign-off that takes the area off a national list. And then the only physical event in the whole film: the marking comes out of the ground. Nothing is added anywhere. Across a longer clock, the whole apparatus is disappearing, because the remaining contaminated area on the island is now small, a national completion strategy has a date on it, and every task closed is one of a countable number left.
place.when_it_looks_best: The dry months, because clearance stops in heavy rain and because the boundary between worked and unworked ground reads hardest when both are dry. Within a day, the first two hours, which are also the working hours here: low sun across a flat country puts the straight edge of the box and the shadow of every stake on the ground, and the tape picks up light. The middle of the day is worth filming for what it takes away, because at noon the box flattens and only the colour difference is left. The closing sequence cannot be scheduled by the film at all: a task is released when it is released, and the crew has to be attached to a task list and take the week the list gives it.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about a rectangle being taken off a map. Worked land from height with one box of untouched scrub in it; a straight edge that no plant would make; tape, stakes, a board with a symbol on it; a lane cut in at right angles; a detector swung in slow arcs; a trowel going in sideways; spoil through a screen; a chalkboard with a number on it that goes up by a few hundred square metres a day; a sampling team walking a grid; forms filled in on a bonnet; and then stakes pulled out of the ground, boards unbolted, tape wound onto a drum, and a vehicle leaving. The last shot is the first shot with nothing in it. It has a complete shape said out loud by nobody, and anyone who likes flat dry country, exact procedure, or the specific satisfaction of a thing being finished properly has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same week becomes the sources' argument about what kind of good release is, and their distinction between a thing held down, a thing pushed aside for a while, and a thing cut off so that it cannot arise again. The texts say the last of those is what matters, and they describe it as a young tree cut down before it fruits: the fruit is not destroyed, it simply never comes. And on the fourth reality itself the film has to do the hardest thing in the group, which is to say plainly what it cannot show. The voice never says this ground is a person, never says a signature is liberation, and never suggests that anybody here has attained anything. It says that the source's own argument for why release is worth more than any pleasure is drawn from ordinary behaviour, that it insists the peace it names is not a feeling, not a place and not a nothing, and that a camera which can show a fence being taken away is exactly the wrong instrument for the thing the texts are pointing at.

sequence.on_screen: First light, high and looking straight down, then tilting out. Ploughed land, paddy, scrub, a tank, a track. In the middle of the frame a rectangle of untouched growth with a dead straight edge, a line of tape along it, and two boards on legs facing outwards.
sequence.voice: Every part of this picture is in use except one, and the difference is not in the soil. The box has been fenced and posted for years. Nothing inside it has been removed yet. What is holding it out of use is a line of tape and a painted board.

sequence.on_screen: Ground level at the boundary. A stake with a painted top, tape strung between two of them, a board carrying a symbol and one word in three scripts. Then the boundary followed along its whole length in one slow move, with worked ground on one side and scrub on the other.
sequence.voice: The sources separate three ways a thing can stop. It can be held down while something stronger keeps it down. It can be pushed aside for a time by putting its opposite in its place. Or it can be cut off at the root, so that it does not come up again [C098-P4:L205–L249]. A fence is the first kind. Everything it does, it stops doing the moment somebody takes it away.

sequence.on_screen: The work at close range and in real time: a lane a metre wide cut in at right angles to the boundary, markers moved forward, a detector head swung in an arc the width of a body, a trowel going in sideways, spoil through a screen, a hand signal, a pause, the same arc again. A chalkboard with a figure on it.
sequence.voice: For the third kind the source gives an image of its own. It compares it to a young tree cut down before it has fruited [C098-P4:L205–L249]. The fruit is not destroyed and it is not forgiven. It simply never comes. What that costs, here, is a figure on a board that goes up by a few hundred square metres a day.

sequence.on_screen: The paper end of it. A sampling team walking a grid across ground that has already been worked. Forms filled in on the bonnet of a vehicle. A signature. A list on a wall with one line on it about to be struck through.
sequence.voice: What finishes here is an obligation with a date on it, and it finishes the way obligations do: somebody walks the ground, somebody confirms that nothing is known to be left, somebody signs, and an area comes off a national list. Nobody is given anything. A line is removed.

sequence.on_screen: The only physical event in the film. Stakes pulled out of the ground and laid in a bundle. Boards unbolted from their legs and stacked in a vehicle. Tape wound onto a drum by hand, metre after metre, until the drum is full and the line along the ground is gone. A vehicle leaving on a sandy track.
sequence.voice: The sources argue for why this kind of good matters more than any pleasure, and they argue it from ordinary behaviour, not from doctrine. People sell land and pawn what they own to be rid of an illness or a debt. Nobody pays that much for nothing, and a person in real pain cannot enjoy wealth or company at all [C073-M:L5–L7]. That is their example, not this film's, and it is the beginning of their argument rather than a case of the thing itself.

sequence.on_screen: One long still frame: the released ground and the ground beside it, in the same shot, indistinguishable. Nothing enters the frame. Then the opening shot repeated exactly, from height, with the rectangle gone out of the picture.
sequence.voice: Here is what this film cannot show you. The texts are describing one reality that is not made by any condition, and they are strict about what it is not. It cannot be felt as a pleasant feeling through the body or the mind at all [C073-P:L18]. It is not produced by effort; it is realised [C073-P:L20]. It has no place, no direction, no material and no shape [C073-P:L62; C073-P:L74]. And it is not nothing, which they say people naturally suspect [C073-P:L50; C073-P:L102]. A camera can show a fence being wound onto a drum. It cannot get anywhere near that.

sequence.on_screen: Last light. The empty country from height, wider than the opening, with no rectangle anywhere in it. A track, a tank, a tree line, and the light going.
sequence.voice: Four things this film is not saying. This ground is not a person and this week is not anybody's life. Nobody in it has attained anything, and the sources are explicit that the change they are describing is a single moment of knowing, produced by a long discipline and not by any event a camera could be present at, and that the persons it makes are not a ladder of levels anybody may be labelled with [C098-M:L5–L7; C098-M:L11–L27]. The film says nothing about why this ground was left as it was, nothing about anybody harmed by it, and nothing about anybody deserving anything. And you cannot reason your way to the thing at the end of this argument; the sources say reasoning gets you an inference and no further [C073-P:L104–L108].

concept_merge.why_together: C073 is the film's subject and C098 is the only thing that makes it filmable. C073 states that the fourth reality is not produced by any condition, is not a pleasant feeling of body or mind [C073-P:L18], is realised rather than manufactured [C073-P:L20], has no location, direction, material or shape [C073-P:L62; C073-P:L74], is nonetheless real and not an empty nothing [C073-P:L50; C073-P:L102], is beyond the reach of reasoning, which yields at most an inference [C073-P:L104–L108], and is one however many realise it [C073-P:L68]. Filmed directly it is unfilmable, and a beautiful still shot offered as a picture of it would be a lie. What the Margaya does supply is an argument, and it argues from ordinary behaviour: people sell land and pawn their belongings to be free of an illness or a debt, which shows what release is worth to them, and a person in severe pain cannot enjoy wealth or family at all [C073-M:L5–L7]. That argument needs a place where an obligation ends, and it needs that place not to be somebody's household. C098 supplies the structure that a place like this can actually carry: the source's three kinds of abandoning, holding down by something stronger, displacing for a time by an opposite, and cutting off at the root so that what was abandoned cannot arise again, with its own image of a young tree cut down before it fruits [C098-P4:L205–L249]. A marked hazardous area is the first kind made physical, since a fence does nothing except while it stands; clearance to full depth with a completion survey and a release is the third; and the difference between them is the whole distinction the source is drawing. C098 also supplies the film's hardest refusals, because it is the concept that forbids labelling any real person and insists the change is a single moment of path-knowledge rather than a course of self-improvement [C098-M:L5–L7; C098-M:L11–L27; C098-P4:L88–L135].
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That release is a category of good on its own, measured by what people will give up to be rid of something rather than by anything it feels like, and that the difference between a burden held back and a burden ended is not a difference of degree. Said flat, the three kinds of abandoning are three technical terms. Put on a fenced rectangle, a lane cut to full depth and a drum of tape carried away, they become the difference between a boundary somebody has to maintain forever and a ground that no longer needs one. The film also earns the group's hardest constraint honestly. Because the last event in it is a removal, and because the released ground is visually identical to the ground next to it, the film reaches the point where it has to say out loud that the thing the texts name cannot be photographed, and can say it over the one frame that makes the claim obvious rather than over a sunset offered as a substitute. This idea has been round once before and was dropped outright rather than relocated. Its previous version filmed a family counting out the last payment on gold pawned years earlier in a hard season: it put a real household's debt, hardship and relief on screen, in a group that carries the divine-eye passages and the protection passages, where a film about hardship ending risks being heard as hardship deserved and its ending as a reward. The concepts are unchanged. What has changed is that there is no household in the film at all, no money, no poverty, nobody's history, and the obligation that ends belongs to an institution, is recorded on paper, and ends in public.

concept_links.why: The film is built on the one part of this concept that can be carried by footage and on the digest's insistence that the rest cannot. The Margaya's argument from behaviour is narrated at the moment the marking is physically removed, and the voice names it as the source's own example and as the beginning of an argument rather than an instance of its conclusion [C073-M:L5–L7]. Then the film does what the group's floor requires of any film that reaches for this concept: it states what it cannot show. Four of the digest's denials are spoken in a single beat, over one long frame of released ground that is indistinguishable from the ground beside it, so that the image cannot be mistaken for the thing: it is not a pleasant feeling of body or mind [C073-P:L18], it is realised and not produced by effort [C073-P:L20], it has no place, direction, material or shape [C073-P:L62; C073-P:L74], and it is not an empty nothing [C073-P:L50; C073-P:L102]. The closing beat adds the limit on reasoning, that argument gives at most an inference [C073-P:L104–L108], which is also the film's own statement about itself. Every limit in the digest that bears on this film is therefore honoured and most of them are on screen. 'Inner peace' as a mood is refused explicitly, and no calm of any person in the film is offered as a pointer to anything. 'A heaven or a place you go' is refused by the denial of location, and the film never lets the released ground stand in as a destination. 'Nothingness' is refused, which matters because the last shot is an absence. 'Achieve your own nirvana' is refused by the realised-not-produced clause, spoken directly over a signature and a drum of tape. The claim that there is one such reality however many realise it is not needed and is not narrated. And the word is never used for the relief of finishing anything, which is the digest's sharpest correction and the exact mistake this location invites.

This concept gives the film its structure and its guard rails. The three kinds of abandoning are narrated in the source's own order over the marking, the fence and the clearance, and the film's central contrast, a boundary that works only while somebody maintains it against ground worked to full depth and signed off, is that distinction and nothing else [C098-P4:L205–L249]. The source's own image for the third kind, a young tree cut down before it fruits, is narrated as the source's picture and not the film's, and the voice adds the digest's own gloss that the fruit is not destroyed and not forgiven but simply never comes [C098-P4:L205–L249]. The digest's limits are then stated out loud in the closing beat, because this group's floor requires them. The noble persons are not a status ladder and no real person may ever be labelled one, so the film labels nobody and says so [C098-M:L11–L27; C098-P4:L88–L135]. The change is not personal growth or self-improvement, and the source's first uprooting is of the belief in a lasting self, so the film does not present the released ground as a better version of itself [C098-P4:L28; C098-P4:L213]. Discipline alone is not the final change, which is why the deminers' skill, patience and composure are never offered as an attainment of any kind. The fruition attainment, the king-at-ease comparison, the counts of person-types and the attainment of cessation are all deliberately unnarrated, both because the footage cannot carry them and because the group's floor forbids letting cessation be heard as switching off or resting [C098-P4:L293; C098-P4:L334–L378; C098-M:L37]. Nothing on screen is presented as a path moment, and the film says in as many words that a single moment of knowing produced by a long discipline is not something a camera can be present at [C098-M:L5–L7].

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That the sources treat being freed from something as a different kind of good from being given something pleasant, and that they argue for it from what people will actually give up to be rid of an illness or a debt; that they distinguish a burden held down or set aside for a time from one cut off so that it cannot arise again, and that only the last of these counts as the change they mean; and that the reality they name at the end of this argument is explicitly not a feeling, not a place and not a nothing, which is why no image in this film or any other can be a picture of it. The ground is an analogy for the shape of an argument and the film says so. Nobody in the film has attained anything, nothing here is anybody's reward, and no claim is made about why this ground was as it was or about anybody affected by it.
what_must_be_real: The task's own work, on the operator's own task list and in its own order and time. No lane is worked twice for the camera, no marking is re-erected after it has come out, no boundary is re-strung, no board is re-hung, no find is re-staged, re-enacted or dramatised, and the release sequence is filmed on the day it happens or not at all. Nothing about how any item is approached, handled or dealt with is altered, repeated or delayed for a shot, and the crew stays outside every boundary the operator sets, at whatever distance it sets, for as long as it says. No casualty, no injury, no survivor and no household's loss is filmed, sought or referred to; the film has no victim in it and makes no claim about anybody harmed. The people working are filmed as people doing work, are not named or followed as characters, are not asked about the war, are not asked to confirm any doctrine, and their composure, patience and skill are never presented as an inner state, an attainment or a lesson. No document is filmed in a way that leaves a landowner's name, address or extent legible, and no land whose ownership, tenure or acquisition is in dispute is filmed at all. The organisation whose task this is decides what may be filmed and retains the right to stop.
position_hint: late in the group, and after at least one film about the discipline and one about seeing clearly: it is the only film in the group that reaches directly for the fourth reality, and it can only do that honestly once the viewer has watched the groundwork that the sources put in front of it. It is also the group's plainest statement that release is a removal rather than an addition, and it closes on the limit of argument, which is the right note to leave the group's biggest claim on. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Letting a signature, a release or a drum of tape be heard as liberation, which is the one substitution this concept's digest forbids most flatly.
Offering a beautiful empty frame as a picture of the unconditioned. The film's answer is to say out loud, over that exact frame, what it cannot show.
Letting the ending read as nothingness or annihilation, when both sources insist the reality they name is real and not an empty nothing.
Turning the deminers into figures of calm, courage or spiritual composure, or letting a viewer read an inner state off a face in a mask.

Drifting into the war: a single archive frame, a casualty figure or a survivor's account would change the film's subject and would put a person's suffering on screen inside a group that must not imply anybody's hardship was deserved.
Filming ground whose ownership, acquisition or tenure is disputed, so that a release becomes an argument about who gets the land.
Sensationalising a find, or building the film towards a moment of danger. The subject is a boundary being removed, not a threat being braved.
Letting the noble persons be heard as levels of progress, or letting the three kinds of abandoning be heard as advice about breaking habits.
Implying that cessation, stopping or switching off is what any of this is about.
Making an institution's procedure look like a ritual, or its paperwork look like a sacrament.
drop_if: No operator and no national authority will allow a task to be filmed from marking through release, since the film is that sequence and its removal.
No release falls inside the filming window, so the film's one event would have to be staged or re-erected.
The only available tasks sit on land whose ownership, acquisition or tenure is in dispute, so filming would put somebody's claim on screen.
Filming cannot be done without altering how any item is approached or handled, or without the crew being anywhere it should not be.
The work can only be filmed in a way that requires a casualty, a survivor or a household to appear in it.
Height cannot be obtained over the area, so the frame that states the concept, a straight-edged box of untouched ground inside worked land, is unavailable.

connections.note: Two films about an ending that consists of removal rather than addition, one on a piece of ground and one at the end of a whole life.
Both turn on the difference between a thing held down and a thing that cannot come back; this one has the distinction written into a procedure with a signature at the end of it.
One film is a range of prepared beginnings standing ready, the other is a single ending being taken off a list.

selection.reason: It is the only place the group has found where an obligation visibly and finally ends with nothing added, and its last frame forces the film to state what it cannot show instead of pretending to show it.

review.note: Rewritten 2026-09-24. The previous version was dropped entirely, not relocated: it filmed a family counting out the last payment on gold pawned years earlier in a hard season, which put a real household's debt, hardship and relief on screen. In a group that carries the divine-eye passages linking low birth and poverty to past deeds, and the passages about the protection of good people, a film about a household's hardship ending would risk being heard as hardship deserved and its ending as a reward, and it also exposed a private financial history to neighbours and other creditors. What was dropped, explicitly: the family, the pawned gold, the instalments, the redemption, the household's years of paying, and every trace of money and poverty. What was kept: both concepts, and the requirement that the place be one where something long owed is finally discharged and the obligation visibly ends. The new subject is a marked hazardous area worked to completion and released: a fence and warning boards that hold ground out of use while they stand, clearance to full depth, a completion survey, a confirmation that nothing is known to remain, a district sign-off that takes the area off a national list, and then the marking itself pulled out of the ground and carried away. The obligation is an institution's, it is recorded on paper, and it ends in public. C073 and C098 were both re-read from the digests as a new reader and every citation re-tested against digest evidence; none was copied from the old record. The group's strictest floor is met head on: the beat that reaches for the fourth reality states, over the one frame that would otherwise be mistaken for it, that it is not a feeling, not produced, not a place and not a nothing, and the film says in as many words that a camera which can show a fence being wound onto a drum cannot get near it. No noble person is labelled, no attainment is claimed, the deminers' composure is never offered as an inner state, cessation is not narrated at all, and the film carries no casualty, no survivor and no household. One further caution is recorded in the location record and in drop_if: parts of this district carry live disputes about acquired land and about a forest-reserve gazette over traditional lands, and a task site inside any such dispute cannot be filmed.

suggested_location.region: Mannar District, Northern Province: the interior of the Musali division in the south of the district, inland of the coast road, in flat thorn-scrub and rain-fed paddy country between small tanks and sandy tracks
suggested_location.why_here: Because this is one of the few districts on the island where the whole sequence still exists to be filmed, and because the remaining work is small enough that a single task is a countable thing rather than a fragment of an industry. The national authority reports about twenty square kilometres of hazardous area left across eleven districts, with this district among the most heavily affected, and a national completion strategy with a date attached to it; so a release here is not routine housekeeping but one of a known and shrinking number of lines to be struck off. The interior of this division gives the film the landscape it needs: flat, open, lightly wooded dry-zone country where worked and unworked ground differ absolutely in colour and texture, so that a marked rectangle reads from the air as a hole in the picture with a straight edge no plant would make. The subject is institutional from end to end. There is a national authority, a district office and international operators, all of which can consent and all of which work to written procedure; there is no household in it, no money in it and no private grief in it; and the one event the film needs, the marking coming out of the ground, happens in the open and is witnessed. The district is thin on this slate. The caution that goes with it is also specific to this district and is recorded below: parts of it carry live disputes over land acquired for other purposes and over a forest-reserve gazette covering lands claimed as traditional, and no task site inside any such dispute can be filmed.
what_to_film: The marked area from height at first light and last light, looking straight down and then tilting out, so the straight edge, the line of tape and the colour difference between worked and unworked ground carry the whole concept in one frame; and the same frame at noon, when the geometry flattens and only the colour is left.

The boundary at working distance: a stake with a painted top, tape between two stakes, a board on legs with its symbol and its word in three scripts, and the boundary followed along its full length in one slow move.

The lane: markers set at intervals, a detector head swung in an arc the width of a body, a prodder going in sideways, spoil going through a screen, a hand signal, a pause, and the same arc again, held long enough that the tedium is the point.
The chalkboard or day sheet with the cleared figure on it, filmed on two different days from the same position.
The quality-assurance sampling: a team walking a grid across ground that has already been worked, at a different pace from the clearance itself.
The paperwork: forms filled in on a bonnet, a signature, and a list with one line about to be struck through, all filmed so that no landowner's name, address or extent is legible.

The removal, in full and in order: stakes pulled and bundled, boards unbolted from their legs and stacked, tape wound onto a drum by hand until the line along the ground is gone, and the vehicle leaving.
One long still frame containing the released ground and the ground beside it, with nothing entering the shot.
The opening aerial frame repeated exactly at the end, with the rectangle absent from the picture.
A boundary elsewhere in the same country that is still standing, filmed in the same light, without commentary.
suggested_location.access: By road south from the district town and then on sandy and gravel tracks. Nothing here can be approached without the national mine action authority and the operator running the task, in writing and in advance, and the operator's rules about distance, boundaries, escorts, footwear, timing and what may be broadcast are absolute and not negotiable by a film. The crew stays outside every boundary the operator sets and follows an escort at all times; nothing on the ground is touched. Drone flight over a task area is not something to assume even though operators use aircraft for their own survey: clearance would have to come from the authority, the operator and the aviation regulator, and it may be refused, in which case the elevated frames have to be obtained from outside the area or not at all. The district secretariat and the divisional secretariat have to agree as well, since the release is an administrative act, and any land whose ownership, acquisition or tenure is contested is out of the question. Work is done early and stops in heavy rain. Everything about the schedule follows the operator's task list, not the film's.
suggested_location.best_time: The dry months, attached to an operator's task list rather than to a calendar, and specifically to a task that is near completion, since the release is the film. A week on the task rather than a day, with a second visit held in reserve for whichever week the completion survey and the removal actually fall in, because neither can be arranged. Within a day, the first two hours, which are both the best light and the working hours, and the middle of the day for the frame in which the geometry disappears.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only, and unverified on the ground. From the national authority's own account of the process: contamination is found and defined by non-technical survey, often because people encountered it while resettling; technical survey then confirms or reduces the boundaries; clearance is carried out by accredited operators to the international standards with quality management alongside it; and an area is released only after a completion survey in which the village officer confirms that no contamination is known and the district authority signs it off. The authority reports 20.51 square kilometres of contamination remaining as of 30 August 2026, names this district among the most heavily affected together with three others, and records that released land in one recent year went mainly to conservation and tourism, then agriculture, then access for resettlement; a national completion strategy covering 2023 to 2027 has been endorsed, and a separate authority notice discusses one large northern minefield being completed by 2027. The division named here is in the south of the district, has its main town at Chilawathurai, covers roughly 475 square kilometres and contains villages including Marichchukkaddi, Mullikulam, Karadikkuli and Periyamurippu. The coordinates are the published position of a small town in that division and are a direction towards the country the film needs, not a survey: no task site, boundary, operator, officer or landowner has been identified or approached, and no permission has been sought from anyone. Three things the film depends on are inferences rather than confirmed facts about this division: that a task here is near completion and will be released inside any plausible filming window, that a crew can be attached to an operator's task list at all, and that height can be obtained over a task area. One political caution is confirmed enough to record: lands in this division are the subject of a public campaign against a gazette declaring traditional lands a forest reserve, and elsewhere in the district there have been protests demanding the release of lands acquired for other projects, so a task site must be checked for any such dispute before anything is filmed. The two images are of mine action work elsewhere in the north, photographed for an aid programme in 2011; no photograph of this division, of a marked area here, or of a release was found on Wikimedia Commons.
